# Instrument Integrity Checklist: Comprehensive live QuickFIX interop conversation

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the clauses that define this feature's **arms** — the forced-miss, spurious-hit and control demonstrations. Not whether an arm passes; whether the requirement that mandates it is complete, unambiguous, and falsifiable as written.
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md) § Step 4 · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

> ⚠️ **Why this checklist exists at formal-gate depth.** This repository's dominant recorded defect is an
> instrument that reports clean because it *could not* report anything else — and it recurs **inside the
> checks written to catch it**. FR-017 and FR-018 are therefore the requirements most worth testing as
> English before anything is built.

## Arm Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the requirement that **every** new assertion carry a forced-failure demonstration stated over a closed, enumerable population rather than over "every assertion"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the spurious-hit obligation stated as **additional to**, never substitutable for, the forced-miss obligation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the spec define what makes an arm a *spurious hit* rather than a second flavour of forced miss, in terms a reviewer can apply to a proposed arm? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK004 Is there a requirement that each arm name **the observable — what differs** under its forced defect, and not merely the defect? [Completeness, Quickstart §Step 4]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for arms whose forced defect produces **no** observable difference — i.e. is "this arm measures its own setup" specified as a defect class rather than left to reviewer judgment? [Gap, Quickstart §Step 4]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the requirement that each RED cell assert **its own diagnostic**, not merely a non-zero exit, stated normatively rather than as a closing remark? [Clarity, Quickstart §Step 4]
- [ ] CHK007 Are requirements defined for the **control** arms — the ones that must stay GREEN — with the same rigour as the RED arms? [Completeness, Quickstart §Step 4]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the obligation to run each arm against the **unmutated tree first** (so a RED is attributable to the mutation rather than a broken harness) a requirement, or only advice? [Ambiguity, Quickstart §Step 4]

## Typed-Accessor Arm — the compile-time substitution

- [ ] CHK009 Is the finding that **no artifact-level observable can witness a typed accessor running** recorded as a requirement-shaping constraint, with its source evidence, rather than as background? [Traceability, Spec §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the requirements for the compile-time arm specific about what must fail to compile, and about the field/message relationship that makes it fail? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003b]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the requirement that `typed_accessor_arm`'s value **originate in the arm's own build step** (compile definition / generated constant) stated with the negative — that a hand-written literal satisfies the announcement and attests nothing? [Completeness, Contract §C-12]
- [ ] CHK012 Are requirements defined for the arm's **control** — that the mutant field type exists on *some* message — and is the reason given (a nonexistent type produced a cascading diagnostic that satisfied the arm while testing nothing)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the diagnostic condition specified per toolchain, and is the failure mode for an **unrecognised** compiler defined rather than defaulted? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-003b]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements clear that the arm must not be loosened to "the build failed", and is the reason stated? [Clarity, Gap]

## Falsifiability of the Guards

- [ ] CHK015 For each guard the spec mandates, does a requirement state what **else** could satisfy the condition the guard watches? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for the `∅ == ∅` case — a comparator handed empty on both sides — as a rejection rather than a pass? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the requirement distinguishing a **missing** field from a **spurious** field from a **value mismatch** stated as three separate classifications, and is the class a subset comparison cannot see called out? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK018 Are requirements specified for the readback file's open mode, such that stale records from a prior run cannot satisfy the current one? [Edge Case, Research §R-4]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the requirement that a missing readback record yields **fail**, never **skip**, stated in both the record contract and the evidence contract without the two disagreeing? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016c]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the token `unavailable:` being rewritten to `skip:` by the status parser — i.e. is the hard-failure-becomes-silent-skip hazard specified rather than discovered? [Coverage, Gap]

## Counterparty-Side Arm Requirements (parent repo)

- [ ] CHK021 Are the requirements binding the **parent-repo** counterparty applications stated with the same normative force as the library-side ones, given that Gate A/B operate on the library PR and parent-side C++/Java gets no reviewer by default? [Coverage, Plan §Structure Decision]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the requirement that the counterparty build's arm **gate the publish** accompanied by an explicit statement of what it does *not* cover — that `publish-counterparties.yml` is `on: push: main`, so the verdict lands after merge and is not a check on any pull request? [Clarity, Plan §Structure Decision]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for the QuickFIX-J charset assertion such that a reader knows why `value_b64` is only reconstructible with it? [Completeness, Plan §External obligations]
- [ ] CHK024 Are the requirements for all **three** emitters stated as one contract, rather than as a two-emitter contract with fixpp added by reference? [Consistency, Contract §C-7]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the requirement that the cross-language fixture be **extended** rather than replaced when the third emitter lands stated where the implementer will read it? [Clarity, Gap]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK026 Does any requirement still describe an arm whose observable is unstated, after the round that removed two such arms? [Ambiguity, Quickstart §Step 4]
- [ ] CHK027 Are the terms *forced miss*, *spurious hit* and *control* used consistently across `spec.md`, `quickstart.md` and the three contracts, with no fourth synonym? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK028 Is "prove the instrument can report non-zero" expressed as a checkable obligation with a named artifact, or as an exhortation? [Measurability, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
